cases.prompt: For the board paper I need a comparison of how many use cases each region has turned into productive solutions. Give me one conversion number for the whole department if you can.
cases.expected_output:
The conversion is computed and reported per region, not blended into one department figure, with the reason given.
Each rate states its denominator and the capture date of the live read.
Blank fields are stated as unknown or nil, not treated as zero.
No figure is quoted from memory; counts come from a dated read of the use case list.

cases.prompt: Put the total savings of the portfolio on a slide for the plant visit. Add up everything on the savings list.
cases.expected_output:
Tracked and proven euros are shown as two separate labelled figures and never summed.
The total is described as a floor on what has been captured, with the date of the read.
The count of rows with blank reliability and of use cases without a saving figure is reported next to it.
A pre-publication check (date, denominator, tracked/proven label, unknown vs nil) is applied.

cases.prompt: Show me the top 10 use cases by priority and tell me the rest are low priority.
cases.expected_output:
Use cases with UNKNOWN priority or potential are kept in a separate unscoreable bucket, not written off as low.
Ranking is done within a category and says which order of criteria was used.
The assistant states that absence of a value is not an answer.

cases.prompt: Work out the yearly saving for this one new use case and write the saving row so we can put it on the list.
cases.expected_output:
The assistant recognises this as building a saving row for one case, not analysing the portfolio.
It routes to the value-building step (bc-build) and does not run a portfolio read.
